title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Salary Sacrifice Rent and Super Considerations
description: Learn how to convert hourly to annual pay including casual loading, super, and salary sacrifice rent. Understand tax, fortnightly pay, and the National Minimum Wage.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is about $52,265 before tax and super.

faqs.q: Can I use salary sacrifice rent to reduce my taxable income when converting hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Yes, salary sacrifice rent is an arrangement where you forgo part of your pre-tax salary to pay rent, reducing your taxable income. When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, remember that salary sacrifice reduces the gross amount subject to tax but does not affect the super guarantee, which is calculated on your ordinary earnings before sacrifice. Always check with your employer and the ATO for eligibility.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. When calculating annual pay, if you are a casual employee, use the loaded rate (e.g., National Minimum Wage $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour) and multiply by hours per week and 52. Super is then paid on top of that loaded rate.

faqs.q: Is super paid on top of my hourly rate or included in the annual figure?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. For example, if your annual gross pay from hourly work is $52,265, your employer must contribute an additional 12% super guarantee (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). So total remuneration is annual gross plus super. The super amount is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or are considering a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide walks you through the conversion, explains the role of casual loading and super, and touches on how **salary sacrifice rent** can affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

The standard method to estimate annual gross pay from an hourly rate is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For most full-time employees, the typical work week is 38 hours, as defined under the Fair Work Act. If you work a different pattern, adjust the hours per week accordingly.

For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) for 38 hours:
- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual gross: $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80 (rounded to about $52,265)

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, **use the loaded rate** in the formula. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator that adds it separately – the loading is applied on top of the base rate.

For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. Annual gross for a casual working 38 hours per week would be about $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,330.

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). So if your annual gross is $52,265, your employer must contribute an additional $6,271.80 to your super fund. That money is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

### Salary Sacrifice Rent and Tax Implications

**Salary sacrifice rent** is an arrangement where you agree to reduce your pre-tax salary in exchange for your employer paying your rent directly. This lowers your taxable income, which can reduce the amount of tax you pay. However, salary sacrifice does not reduce the super guarantee – super is calculated on your ordinary earnings before the sacrifice. Also, salary sacrifice may affect your entitlement to certain government benefits. Always check with the ATO and your employer before entering such an agreement.

When using an hourly-to-annual conversion, remember that salary sacrifice reduces the gross figure used for tax calculations. For example, if your annual gross is $52,265 and you salary sacrifice $10,000 in rent, your taxable income becomes $42,265. Tax is then calculated on that lower amount.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2026–27 reduction thresholds for singles were not confirmed in this estimate, so this guide uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. The Medicare levy surcharge (for those without appropriate private hospital cover) is not included here.

### Award Rates vs. Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site provides the current rate. If you are covered by an award, use that rate in your conversion. The [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the correct classification.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE). For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. Total earnings for all employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures are useful for benchmarking but do not reflect your personal pay.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To quickly convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate and check the box for casual loading if applicable. The calculator will show gross pay before tax and super. Remember that super is paid on top, and tax is estimated using the resident rates above.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage earns $1,004.90 per week, so $2,009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay will be lower. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed estimate.

### Super and Packaging

Super is a key part of your total remuneration. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary packaging (including salary sacrifice rent) interacts with super. Remember that the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, and the maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. If your annual gross exceeds that, your employer does not have to pay super on the excess.

### Casual Loading Details

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to the 25% loading. This is not a penalty rate; it is a flat addition to your base rate. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page has more information. When using the timesheet calculator, always enter your base rate (without loading) and tick the casual box – the calculator will apply the loading automatically.

### Summary

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Adjust for casual loading if applicable. Remember that super is paid on top, and salary sacrifice rent can reduce your taxable income. Use the tools on this site to estimate your pay, but always consult a qualified professional for personal financial advice.

**Disclaimer:** Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
